support: ILO reports around 11.5 million workers in Viet Nam, about one in five workers, are in occupations with tasks potentially exposed to GenAI.
ILO reports roughly one million workers are in occupations where tasks are highly susceptible and standardized, less than 2% of the workforce.
ILO's review concludes productivity gains are real but uneven and large-scale job displacement remains limited in the empirical evidence reviewed.
ILO highlights erosion of employment opportunities for younger workers among the main emerging risks.
BLS projects software developers from 1,717,800 jobs in 2025 to 1,892,600 in 2035: +174,700, or +10.2%.
BLS projects computer programmers from 110,800 jobs in 2025 to 102,700 in 2035: -8,100, or -7.3%, and explicitly notes automation of repetitive programming tasks including AI.
OECD Skills for Jobs 2026 across 38 countries finds persistent shortages concentrated in high-skilled occupations, notably ICT, health and teaching professionals.
OECD states that U.S. ICT professional shortages intensified after the launch of ChatGPT in 2022.
IMF analyzes 40 million online job postings across 19 Asian economies and finds employer demand fell by nearly 10% in more AI-exposed occupations relative to less-exposed ones.
IMF reports the relative demand decline appears to have stabilized even as AI capability improved rapidly.
IMF reports rising employer demand for workers with AI skills.
